description: You are a Security Engineer at a company that has recently observed early-stage ransomware indicators on the network. Your SIEM (Wazuh) needs a complete ransomware detection and automated response capability. When complete, the Wazuh configuration must include: (1) File Integrity Monitoring enabled on at least three critical Linux filesystem paths (e.g. /home, /etc, /var/www, or similar high-value directories); (2) at least one custom detection rule at severity level 10 or higher that identifies ransomware-associated activity such as shadow copy deletion, mass file modification, or suspicious file extension creation; (3) a frequency-based correlation rule using Wazuh's frequency and timeframe rule attributes that triggers on repeated ransomware-related events within a time window; (4) an active-response block configured in ossec.conf that takes automated action on critical ransomware detections; and (5) a written incident response playbook saved to /home/ga/Desktop/ransomware_playbook.txt of at least 600 characters documenting the detection logic and response procedures. The environment already has pre-seeded ransomware-precursor events in the alert feed. Log in to the Wazuh dashboard at https://localhost with username admin, password SecretPassword.
